I am 62 years old and have been working this land in Quzhou for 40 years. I know every mu of my 15 mu farm, and I know what my body can still handle alone. My well gives me water, but pumping costs money, so I do not waste a drop.

My winter wheat went into the ground last October after ploughing. It is up now and needs top-dressing with urea and an irrigation at jointing. I will irrigate two more times if the sky stays dry—once at flowering and once at grain filling. I use an improved wheat variety that my neighbor saved seed from; it is reliable. I will spray twice: once for weeds and once if I see aphids or rust. I expect about 460 kg per mu. That wheat comes off in early June, and I immediately rotary till and plant hybrid maize. Summer maize grows fast; it needs two irrigations and two sprays, and should give me over 500 kg per mu. Hybrid seed is expensive, but the yield gain pays for itself.

I keep 6 mu for stevia because it brings good cash, though it is hard work for an old man. I will hire a few villagers to help transplant seedlings in early May. Stevia needs fertile soil, so I rotary till the beds and put down compound fertilizer—less nitrogen than wheat, but more potassium so the leaves stay sweet. I will irrigate five times through the season and spray three times for leaf spot and insects. I expect about 200 kg of dry leaves per mu. I do not grow more stevia because 6 mu is all I can manage with my back and my well.

Here is my plan for the year:
